//Serilog: REQ-NFR-001 / REQ-NFR-029 - overrides for the logger built in Program.cs. Information by default; the per-component render-tree Debug logging that cost ~61 KB per request is enabled only by appsettings.Development.json.
//LogFile: REQ-NFR-029 - the rolling file sink. Path is a DIRECTORY (the file name carries Serilog's date and sequence suffixes) and is resolved against AppContext.BaseDirectory when relative or absent, NOT against the working directory - a bare relative path is what put 6.2 MB in the repository-root logs/ and 305 MB in source/TechieBlog/logs/ for one application on one day. WORST CASE TOTAL DISK = SizeLimitBytes * RetainedFileCountLimit = 10 MB * 10 = 100 MB per host. The previous 50 MB * 7 = 350 MB is what that 305 MB actually was: retention working exactly as configured. Capping a FILE is not capping a DISK - change either number only with the product in mind. Set LogFileEnabled=false in a container, where the file lands in an ephemeral layer and Docker already captures stdout.
//Seq: REQ-NFR-013 - centralised logging. DELIBERATELY EMPTY here: the Seq sink is attached only when Seq:Url is set, so a fresh clone runs with no Seq server and no connection errors. The deployment supplies SeqUrl=http://seq:5341 and SeqApiKey from a secret; the API key is a live ingestion credential and must never be committed to this file.
//Uploads: REQ-FN-025 - Uploads:Path names the directory that uploaded media is written to and served from at /uploads. DELIBERATELY EMPTY here: unset means wwwroot/uploads, which is the clone-and-run default. A CONTAINER MUST SET IT (UploadsPath=/app/uploads, bound to a host volume) because wwwroot lives inside the image and a redeploy would delete every image an editor has ever uploaded. See BlogEngine.Storage.UploadsLocation.
//ForwardedHeaders: REQ-NFR-028 - explicit proxy allow-list. EMPTY means nothing is trusted and X-Forwarded-For is ignored, which is correct for a direct-to-Kestrel deployment. Behind nginx or a load balancer, list that proxy's address in KnownProxies (or its subnet in KnownNetworks, CIDR form) in the environment-specific settings file. NEVER use 0.0.0.0/0 - a blanket trust lets any caller forge its own rate-limit identity.
//Secrets: REQ-NFR-027 - JwtSigningKey and AppEncryptionKey are deliberately ABSENT from this file. Supply them through user secrets or the environment; the host refuses to start without them and has no fallback default.
//SiteSettings: REQ-NFR-030 - SiteSettings:BaseUrl is deliberately ABSENT from this file. It used to read https://localhost:5001, which is read once at construction by NewsletterSvc, EmailVerificationSvc, SitemapSvc and RssFeedSvc - so a real deployment that never changed it mailed unsubscribe links pointing at its own loopback address, silently, with no error raised. Supply the site's public origin per deployment: dotnet user-secrets set "SiteSettings:BaseUrl" "https://blog.example.com" (or SiteSettings__BaseUrl in the environment). A non-Development host REFUSES TO START without it; appsettings.Development.json carries a loopback value for local work and the host logs one loud warning about it.
//Analytics: REQ-NFR-030 - Analytics:VisitorSalt is a DEPLOYMENT SECRET and must never be committed. It is the salt in SHA-256(salt|ip|userAgent); with a salt an attacker knows, the digest is reversible across the whole IPv4 space and PostViewTracker's pseudonymous visitor becomes a record of who read what. Supply at least 32 random characters: dotnet user-secrets set "Analytics:VisitorSalt" "$(openssl rand -hex 32)". TREAT IT AS WRITE-ONCE - rotating it resets every stored visitor pseudonym. A non-Development host REFUSES TO START without it.
